steps.name: Sample structure QC (low-depth and duplication audit)
caveats: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

If a sample has a high duplication rate, do not remove the duplicate reads unless the library carries unique molecular identifiers. In RNA-seq the duplication rate follows the expression level, because a highly expressed gene gives many identical fragments. Thus removal without UMIs deletes true signal, and it does not improve the differential expression result. Report the duplication rate of each sample beside its library size and its detected genes. A duplication rate far above the others in a low-depth library is a sign of low complexity, and then the sample is a candidate outlier with a stated reason.
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-with-total-rna-highdup-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples: one gene-id column plus 12 sample columns) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-total-rna-highdup-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows: sample, condition; 6 treated, 6 control). Libraries are rRNA-depleted total RNA without UMIs; sequencing QC reports duplication rate above 60% in most libraries; sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median. The record does not state whether the Salmon output carried a length correction: verify and record the count-table state (integer raw counts vs fractional/length-corrected abundance — both are valid for the downstream count model; a pure TPM scale with all sample totals near 1e6 would be invalid and must be flagged, not modeled as counts).

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm LFC shrinkage (primary)
caveats: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
steps.context: Same inputs as T1S1. The input is a gene-level Salmon table with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript-length table: the import state is not established and the length offset is lost, so fit the count model on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and state this in the outputs. Do not run tximport on a gene table, and do not invent a length input. Set the condition factor explicitly with reference level 'control'; contrast numerator 'treated', denominator 'control' (positive log2FC = higher in treated). n=6 per group: DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cook's distance and sets the p-value and adjusted p-value of those genes to NA — keep this behavior on and report the count of such genes separately from genes removed by filtering. Design: ~condition, unpaired, single batch, no covariates.

plan.title: Heart treated vs control bulk RNA-seq DE
plan.analytical_narrative: Twelve human heart libraries (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch) from rRNA-depleted total-RNA libraries without UMIs, with a gene-level Salmon count table (12,000 genes x 12 samples). QC reports >60% duplication in most libraries and sample_01 ~4x below the median library size, so the first step is sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA on top-500 variable genes, distance heatmap) that keeps and inspects sample_01 rather than deleting it, and reports duplication rates without UMI-based removal. Because only the gene-level table was delivered — no per-sample quantifications and no average transcript-length table — the Salmon length offset cannot be reconstructed; the count model is therefore fit on the counts as delivered without a length offset, and the lost offset is stated as a limitation (isoform-use changes can appear as DE). DESeq2 (Wald test, apeglm LFC shrinkage, minimal pre-filter, independent filtering, BH at FDR 0.05) is the primary model; the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test runs on the identical gene and sample set as the second method, and the report treats their intersection as the high-confidence set. With 6 replicates per group, DESeq2 Cook's-distance outlier handling stays in flag mode (NA p-values), and those genes are reported separately.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst blind, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
gene counts without length offset, explicit reference level

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

If a sample has a high duplication rate, do not remove the duplicate reads unless the library carries unique molecular identifiers. In RNA-seq the duplication rate follows the expression level, because a highly expressed gene gives many identical fragments. Thus removal without UMIs deletes true signal, and it does not improve the differential expression result. Report the duplication rate of each sample beside its library size and its detected genes. A duplication rate far above the others in a low-depth library is a sign of low complexity, and then the sample is a candidate outlier with a stated reason.

A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
